title: Finite-type flatness gives a finitely presented etale neighborhood
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and let $x\in X$ with $s=f(x)$ such that $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then there are an elementary etale neighbourhood $(S',s')\to(S,s)$ (an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s')$ of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]) and an open subscheme $V\subset X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{S',s'})$ [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-open-immersion] containing the unique point $x'$ over $x$ such that the pullback of $\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] to $V$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and flat over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over].

source.place: Tag 05I6, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof (affine reduction and induction).

proof.text: Restrict to affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $s$. If $x\notin\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, then $\mathcal F_x/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal F_x=0$. The stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is finite over the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and $\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is contained in its maximal ideal. Nakayama gives $\mathcal F_x=0$. Apply the surjective-on-stalk lemma to $0\to\mathcal F$: it is surjective on a neighbourhood, so $\mathcal F$ vanishes there. The identity neighbourhood of $S$ then works, since the zero module has an empty finite presentation and is flat. Otherwise put $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$ and use strong induction on $n\ge0$. This is finite: the affine fibre is of finite type over $\kappa(s)$, hence has finite dimension, and its support has dimension at most that of the fibre.

Bookkeeping for local bases. One may replace a pointed base $(T,t)$ by $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}$ during the induction. Indeed this spectrum is the directed inverse limit of the affine open neighbourhoods of $t$, with affine transitions and all stages qcqs. An affine etale neighbourhood of finite presentation over that local spectrum descends to an etale scheme of finite presentation over one such open, by the object clause of etale finite-data descent. Its marked point has the same residue field as its image on that open, since the fibre at $t$ is unchanged by localization. Its local ring is the same as the marked local ring before descent. Thus a further elementary etale change of a local base is realized by an elementary etale change of the preceding scheme, with the same final local base. Composing these finitely many changes is etale by composition, and the residue-field isomorphisms compose. The neighbourhood in the conclusion only lives over the final local ring, so no spreading of the possibly non-finitely-presented sheaf is being asserted.

Apply elementary module devissage to $f,\mathcal F,x$ (locally finite presentation implies locally finite type). It gives affine $X',Z',Y',S'$, elementary etale $g,e$, a finitely presented closed immersion $i$, a finite map $\pi$ with singleton marked fibre, and $\mathcal G$ with $i_*\mathcal G=g^*\mathcal F$; $Y'\to S'$ is smooth with geometrically integral fibres of dimension $n$. Replace the base by $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S',s'}$. The comparison $X'\to X\times_SS'$ is etale by cancellation between schemes etale over $X$, hence its base change to $T$ is etale. The other diagram properties persist: the defining closed-immersion ideal has finitely many generators, a finite algebra remains finite after tensor product, and the marked fibres are unchanged because $\kappa(s')$ is unchanged. Finite presentation of the affine structure maps survives tensor base change. Smoothness survives base change and geometric integrality is defined after arbitrary residue-field extension. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence and finite type, and affine pushforward commutes with this base change, preserving $i_*\mathcal G=g^*\mathcal F$ and identifying the base change of $\pi_*\mathcal G$ with the new finite pushforward.

The devissage flatness equivalence shows that the finite pushforward $\pi_*\mathcal G$ is flat at $y'$ over the local base; the finite-pushforward lemma makes it quasi-coherent of finite type. The devissage finite-presentation equivalence applies because $f$ is locally of finite presentation. Both equivalences concern properties on actual neighbourhoods, not merely finite presentation or flatness of an isolated stalk. They therefore reduce the desired conclusion to that for $\pi_*\mathcal G$ on $Y'$. The equivalences can also be applied after any further elementary etale base change followed by localization: the same affine diagram, singleton marked fibre and residue fields persist as in step 3. We are consequently reduced to $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ local, $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ smooth over $A$, with geometrically integral fibres of dimension $n$, and $\mathcal F=\widetilde N$ for a finite $B$-module. Write $\mathfrak m$ for the maximal ideal of $A$ and $\mathfrak q$ for $x$. Smoothness makes $A\to B$ flat and finitely presented, and $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat.

The integral closed fibre $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak mB)$ has generic prime $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak mB$. The images of a finite generating list of $N$ span the finite-dimensional vector space $N\otimes_B\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Select a basis from this spanning list and lift its elements by the corresponding generators of $N$. They define $\alpha:B^r\to N$ inducing an isomorphism at $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; allow $r=0$ if that vector space is zero.

Apply the local generic-basis universal-injectivity criterion to $R=A$, $S=B$, $\xi=\mathfrak p$ and the chosen $\alpha$. Its hypotheses are exactly flat finite presentation with geometrically integral fibres, $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak m$, finiteness of $N$, flatness of $N_{\mathfrak q}$ over $A$, and the residue-field basis from step 5. Thus $\alpha$ is $A$-universally injective and $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat for $Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$. In particular $0\to B^r\to N\to Q\to0$ is exact, and remains left exact after every base change of $A$.

The module $Q$ is finite, and $(Q/\mathfrak mQ)_{\mathfrak p}=0$: reduce the chosen basis isomorphism at $\mathfrak p$ and use right exactness of tensor products. Its support is a proper closed subset of the integral $n$-dimensional closed fibre. Here closedness can be checked directly: for a finite generating list, vanishing at a prime means a product of denominators outside that prime kills every generator; hence support equals the zero locus of its annihilator. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of this proper closed subset extends by appending the whole integral fibre, so its length is at most $n-1$. Consequently the dimension at $\mathfrak q$ of this support is $<n$ whenever it is nonempty. For $n=0$ the support is empty.

If $Q_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak mQ_{\mathfrak q}=0$ (in particular in dimension zero), Nakayama over $B_{\mathfrak q}$ gives $Q_{\mathfrak q}=0$, and the finite-type surjective-on-stalk lemma shrinks to a principal open $D(g)$ containing $\mathfrak q$ on which $Q_g=0$. Otherwise apply the strong induction hypothesis to $\widetilde Q$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at $\mathfrak q$: it is finite type, the morphism is locally finitely presented, $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat by step 6, and its fibre-support dimension is strictly smaller by step 7. It gives a further elementary etale local base and an open neighbourhood where the pullback of $Q$ is finitely presented and flat. Shrink that neighbourhood to a principal $D(g)$ about the marked point. Rename the new base and modules $A,B,N,Q$; sections on this affine open give $Q_g$ finitely presented over $B_g$ and $A$-flat. Universal injectivity from step 6 and exactness of localization give $0\to B_g^r\to N_g\to Q_g\to0$.

Put $R=B_g$. The module $R$ is flat over $A$ because $D(g)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a restriction of the smooth morphism, and $Q_g$ is $A$-flat. To prove $N_g$ flat, let $U\hookrightarrow V$ be any injection of $A$-modules. The flat-quotient tensor lemma gives exact rows $0\to U\otimes_A R^r\to U\otimes_A N_g\to U\otimes_A Q_g\to0$ and the analogous row for $V$. The outer vertical maps are injective by flatness. An element in the kernel of the middle vertical map maps to zero on the right, hence comes from the left; injectivity on the left and exactness of the lower row make that lift zero. Thus the middle map is injective, which is precisely $A$-flatness of $N_g$.

proof.text: For finite presentation of $N_g$, choose $R^a\to R^b\to Q_g\to0$. Lift the $b$ generators to $N_g$ and adjoin the $r$ generators of its submodule $R^r$. For each of the $a$ generating relations of $Q_g$, its lifted combination lies in $R^r$; subtract its unique expression in that basis. These $a$ relations generate the kernel of the resulting surjection $R^{b+r}\to N_g$: any kernel vector first projects to a relation of $Q_g$, so subtract a combination of the chosen lifted relations, leaving a relation in the injected free submodule, hence zero. This is a finite presentation of $N_g$. Its associated sheaf on $D(g)$ therefore has a finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 05I5 first proof, last paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 0519 (extension), part (2), with the presentation argument written out

proof.text: We have solved the smooth case, including $n=0$. Transfer its finitely presented neighbourhood and its flat neighbourhood back through the devissage using the two neighbourhood equivalences, and intersect the resulting opens about the marked point; both properties persist under restriction. This gives the required $V$ in the base change of the original $X$ to the final local base. Step 2 realizes all base changes as a single elementary etale neighbourhood $(S',s')\to(S,s)$. Finally the points above $x$ in the base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S',s'}$ are the points of $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})$. This tensor product is $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(s')=\kappa(x)$: the closed fibre of the local etale map is its residue field and $\kappa(s')=\kappa(s)$. Thus this point is unique, as required.
